ms.report:
We have completed Milestone 1 for "Regulated and Permissioned DeFi with Sundae and Kora Labs." This milestone provides a detailed specification on attaching a Decentralized Identifier (DID) to an ADA Handle and how services can resolve that DID to enable secure, regulated transactions on the Cardano blockchain.
Milestone 1 Deliverables
・Specification for DID Attachment: Instructions on linking a DID to an ADA Handle, allowing decentralized services to resolve identity information securely.
・DID Resolution: A step-by-step process for how a service can resolve a DID using an ADA Handle.
・Clarification on CIP-30 Extension: Originally, we intended to extend CIP-30 to include DID request capabilities. However, after further exploration, we determined that the dApp can resolve the DID directly via the ADA Handle without needing the wallet to perform the lookup. This change simplifies the implementation and increases overall efficiency. Consequently, we did not proceed with the CIP-30 extension as originally planned. Instead, the project team will leverage the Cardano Foundation’s wallet and existing standards such as KERI and IPEX for future credential verification functionalities, which are beyond the scope of this milestone.

Evidence of Milestone Completion
・Specification Document: The full specification can be found here with detailed steps on how a dApp can resolve a DID using an ADA Handle (Section 2, Page 3): https://github.com/SundaeSwap-finance/sundae-specs/blob/main/permissioned-pool/spec.pdf
・Announcements: We have made announcements on our social platforms:
・https://x.com/SundaeSwap/status/1842577688352956837
・https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O2XYygU4Fu5CfF8GjbBtutgZoNErOr12/view?usp=sharing

Note on Changes in Approach
As mentioned above, we initially planned to extend CIP-30 but realized that it wasn’t necessary for this specific use case. The dApp can resolve the DID from the ADA Handle without wallet involvement, making the process simpler for developers.

ms.report:
This final close-out report outlines the completion of the Permissioned DeFi Pools project by Sundae Labs, with collaboration from Kora Labs. The work focused on building a testnet-deployed proof of concept for permissioned liquidity pools on Cardano and drafting a robust technical specification for identity-based access logic using decentralized identifiers (DIDs) and ADA Handles.
The report includes detailed discussion of key project KPIs, including public technical specifications, testnet deployment, and published milestone announcements. While the joint nature of the project posed scheduling and coordination challenges, the technical goals were met successfully.
Key learning outcomes include:
・The difficulty of coordinating joint Catalyst projects across two teams with separate internal priorities and timelines.
・The realization that identifying a customer earlier in the process would have helped focus and guide development.

As noted in the close-out video, the team has demonstrated that permissioned DeFi is feasible on Cardano, and the next stage is identifying use cases and customers who need it.
This submission includes a summary report, links to GitHub specifications, working testnet transactions, public milestone announcements, and a short video walk-through. These materials collectively demonstrate that the proposal's deliverables have been completed and publicly shared.
Final Report: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1F9nd8rrVUQ53usmQsTgt4ODDwDMeSpDU/view
Wrap Up Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aTPdOUfCDC8
